exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 At the Forbidden City
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Tourist: Excuse me, could you please tell me about this old mirror?
Guide: Of course. It is said that this mirror can tell right from wrong.
Tourist: How interesting! And what is that carving on the roof?
Guide: That is called chiwen, one of the nine sons of the Chinese dragon.
Tourist: I have never heard of it. Is this palace very old?
Guide: Yes. It was built hundreds of years ago and is an important heritage site.
Tourist: Thank you. I really want to help protect places like this.
Guide: That's wonderful. Every visitor who cares can make a difference.
exercises.translation_cn: 游客请向导介绍一面古镜;向导说这镜子据说能分辨是非;游客又问屋顶上的雕刻;那叫鸱吻,是中国龙的九子之一;宫殿建于数百年前,是重要遗产地;游客想帮忙保护这样的地方;向导说每个用心的游客都能起作用。

questions.stem: What does the guide say about the old mirror?
options: It can tell right from wrong.

questions.stem: What is the carving on the roof called?
How old is the palace?
What does the tourist want to do?
What does the guide say about caring visitors?
options: Each one can make a difference.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 What Is Cultural Heritage
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Cultural heritage is what we receive from the past.
It includes temples, relics, and ancient buildings.
But it also includes customs, dances, and old crafts.
We live with this heritage today and pass it on to the future.
Protecting it is the duty of every one of us.
exercises.translation_cn: 文化遗产是我们从过去继承下来的;它包括庙宇、文物和古建筑;但也包括习俗、舞蹈和古老的手工艺;我们今天与这份遗产共存,并把它传给未来;保护它是我们每个人的责任。

questions.stem: Where does cultural heritage come from?
Which of these is part of heritage, according to the passage?
What do we do with this heritage today?
options: We live with it and pass it on.

questions.stem: Whose duty is it to protect heritage?
What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Cultural heritage is broad and worth protecting.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Interview at the Youth Camp
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Reporter: Hello, can you tell me what your camp is doing at Mount Tai?
Student: Sure. We are high school students from seven different countries.
Reporter: That's amazing. What exactly are you creating?
Student: We are making an app to introduce the mountain to young people.
Reporter: Why did you choose an app?
Student: Because it is a fun and easy way to share its history.
Reporter: Do you do anything besides the app?
Student: Yes, we visit local schools to talk about protecting heritage.
exercises.translation_cn: 记者问营地在泰山做什么;学生说他们是来自七个国家的高中生;他们在制作一个向年轻人介绍泰山的应用;选择应用是因为它有趣又容易分享历史;除了应用,他们还去当地学校宣传保护遗产。

questions.stem: Where are the students from?
What are the students creating?
Why did they choose an app?
options: It is a fun, easy way to share history.

questions.stem: What else do the students do?
options: They visit local schools to talk about heritage.

questions.stem: What is the students' main goal?
options: To share the mountain's history with young people.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Three Ways to Help
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here are three simple ways to protect cultural heritage.
First, never touch or damage old relics when you visit them.
Second, learn the stories behind them and share what you know.
Third, join a group of volunteers near you.
Even small actions can help save our treasures.
exercises.translation_cn: 这里有三个保护文化遗产的简单方法;第一,参观时绝不触碰或损坏古老文物;第二,了解它们背后的故事并分享;第三,加入身边的志愿者团体;即使微小的行动也能帮助拯救我们的珍宝。

questions.stem: What is the first piece of advice?
options: Never touch or damage old relics.

questions.stem: What is the second piece of advice?
options: Learn the stories and share them.

questions.stem: What is the third piece of advice?
How many ways does the passage give?
What does the passage say about small actions?
options: They can help save our treasures.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Raising Money for the Temple
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Anna: Our committee needs to raise more money to repair the old temple.
Ben: How much have we collected so far?
Anna: Only half of what we need. The roof is in danger.
Ben: Maybe we could ask different departments to contribute.
Anna: Good idea. We could also invite the public to donate.
Ben: I can write a letter to ask local companies for help.
Anna: Perfect. If we work together, I'm sure we can save it.
Ben: Let's start today. There is no time to lose.
exercises.translation_cn: Anna 说委员会要为修庙筹更多钱;Ben 问已筹多少;只筹到一半,屋顶有危险;Ben 建议请各部门捐助;Anna 说也可邀请公众捐款;Ben 愿写信向本地公司求助;两人决定齐心就能拯救它;立刻就动手,刻不容缓。

options: Only half of what they need.

options: Write a letter to local companies.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Help from the United Nations
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Sometimes a problem is too big for one country alone.
When ancient temples were in danger, one nation asked the world for help.
A committee was set up to limit the damage.
Many countries gave money and sent their best experts.
Together, they proved that great challenges can lead to great solutions.
exercises.translation_cn: 有时一个问题对单个国家来说太大;当古庙陷入危险时,一个国家向世界求助;成立了一个委员会以减少损害;许多国家出钱并派出最优秀的专家;他们共同证明,巨大的挑战能带来伟大的解决方案。

questions.stem: When is a problem too big for one country?
options: When it is very large and difficult.

questions.stem: What did one nation do when the temples were in danger?
options: It asked the world for help.

questions.stem: What was the committee set up to do?
How did many countries help?

questions.stem: What did the countries prove together?
options: Temples should be left to fall.
